Subject: Cutover readiness: ops acceptance, surge throttles, and fallback lanes

Team / Acme ops —

This is the penultimate readiness note ahead of the scheduled VPC/on‑prem cutover this Friday. High level asks before we greenlight the activation window:

- Confirm network gating ACLs are applied (east-west and cross‑DC).
- Confirm KV cache priming procedure (order + expected warmup token counts).
- Finalize surge throttle thresholds and the immediate fallback lanes we will route to if latency > 350ms for 3+ minutes.
- Ensure telemetry mappings in the attached matrix match the runbook event ids.

Attachments: [attachment: runbook_v3.pdf (PDF)], [attachment: telemetry_matrix.csv (CSV)]

Pushing for a concise signoff today so we can publish the activation email to the wider ops roster. If Acme wants the bridge window changed, call it out here; otherwise the plan remains: Friday 2027‑09‑03 02:00–05:00 UTC (low traffic).

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cutover readiness: ops acceptance, surge throttles, and fallback lanes

Alex —

Network gating verification complete from our side:
- East‑west ACLs applied to the VPC peering subnets (10.48.0.0/16).
- BGP advertisements confirmed; edge‑to‑edge routes are present and next‑hop healthy.
- Test traffic passed HTTP 200 checks across both NICs; small packet loss observed on nic-2 for a 2‑minute window (investigating).

I flagged the nic-2 loss in the runbook notes (section 4.2). Recommend a pre‑cutover quick restart of the switch agent if we still see any flapping during the scheduled window.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
From: ops@acmecorp.com

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 13:40:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Cutover readiness: ops acceptance, surge throttles, and fallback lanes

Thanks Alex & team — quick notes from Acme DevOps:

- We will run a KV priming sweep tonight against the staging cluster that mirrors the pattern in runbook_v3. Expect a 35–45 minute warmup for ~180M tokens; please confirm this matches Redwood's estimates.
- Concern: the proposed surge throttle to fall back to the shared cached pool will increase tail latency for some enterprise customers. Can we limit the fallback to non‑SLA tenants for the first 30 minutes after failover?
- Can Colin Bates from EdgeCloud be looped on the BGP route dampening strategy? He can propose a protective policy. c.c. colin.bates@edgecloud.io

We will post the warmup logs to the shared Drive link and flag anything anomalous.

—Acme DevOps (ops@acmecorp.com)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, ops@acmecorp.com, colin.bates@edgecloud.io
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cutover readiness: ops acceptance, surge throttles, and fallback lanes

Acme / team —

Responding to the priming numbers & fallback scope:

- Confirmed: Redwood estimate for full KV priming in that traffic pattern is 30–50 minutes. Expect initial heat to reduce token latency by ~22% once primed.
- Fallback lanes: we will implement a two‑tier fallback —
  * Tier A (sensitive tenants): only allowed after full on‑call approval and will route to dedicated reserved pool.
  * Tier B (non‑SLA / dev tenants): automatic fallback to shared cached pool at threshold breach.
- For the first 30 minutes post‑failover, the policy will be to keep Tier A pinned to reserved instances; Tier B will be eligible for automated redirection.

I've attached a small diagram that maps the fallback lanes to the VPC subnets and the route‑map ids. Please review and confirm.

Attachments: [attachment: fallback-lanes-diagram.png (PNG)]

Operational notes for the bridge:
- Bridge will open 15 minutes before traffic shift; runbook stage 'PRE-PRIME' must be green.
- Guardrails: automated throttle rollback if error rate > 1.2% for 5 minutes or P95 latency > 700ms.

If Acme wants Tier A policy tightened further we can require multi‑party signoff via the DocuSign path in related_links.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Principal PM, Deployments | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Cutover readiness: ops acceptance, surge throttles, and fallback lanes — final preflight

All —

Thanks for the fast turnarounds. Final checklist before I publish the activation notice:

1) Irene — confirm switch agent on nic-2 either remediated or scheduled for 30min prewindow restart.
2) Mina — confirm routing policies and route‑map ids deployed to the fabric (use the attached diagram ids).
3) Marcus — confirm telemetry alerts wired to PagerDuty with runbook stage ids (PRE-PRIME, PRIME, SHIFT, ROLLBACK).
4) Acme — confirm you completed the KV priming run and uploaded logs to the Drive link.

If all green by EOD PDT tomorrow I will:
- Publish the activation email to both companies' bridges;
- Start the bridge 15 minutes before the window as Lauren noted;
- Monitor P95 and error budget, and trigger Tier B fallback if thresholds breached.

Link to runbook & signoff: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-runbook-v3
DocuSign: https://docsign.example.com/tx/ACME-CUTOFF-9876

Thanks —
Alex
